title: A Mechanism of Weak-to-Strong Generalization: Feature Elicitation from Latent Knowledge
claim: Training with weak supervision elicits the target feature quickly and smoothly, while standard fine-tuning is far slower and abrupt, with different effects on other neurons.
layout: 2x2+ grid of line plots, rows W2S vs SFT, columns by task
description: A grid of line plots showing per-neuron absolute alignment between hidden-unit weights and a task's feature direction over training steps. Rows are the training regimes, W2S on top and SFT on the bottom. Columns are tasks, with the left column titled 'target task (k=1)' and further columns cut off on the right. Each plot has many thin curves, one per neuron. Dark purple solid lines mark neurons that align with the target, and red and orange dotted lines mark other neurons. Faint grey lines are the rest. In the W2S panel the alignment of several neurons rises smoothly to about 1 over 10,000 steps. In the SFT panel the neurons jump sharply at staggered times, over a horizontal axis of about 2e7 steps. The eye goes first to the dark purple curves climbing toward 1.0.
caption: Per-neuron alignment magnitude |θ⊤
abstract: Weak-to-strong (W2S) generalization, in which a strong model is fine-tuned on outputs of a weaker, task-specialized model, has been proposed as an approach to aligning superhuman AI systems. Existing theoretical analyses either fix the student's representations or operate in restricted settings. Whether multi-step SGD can succeed in feature learning while preserving diverse pre-trained capabilities remains open. We study W2S in the setting of reward-model learning with two-layer neural networks. The strong model has pre-trained representations organized into low-dimensional subspaces $V_k$, and is fine-tuned under the supervision of a weak model specialized on task $Îº$. We prove that the strong model efficiently learns task $Îº$, eliciting its pre-trained knowledge while retaining general capabilities. This establishes W2S generalization in the feature-learning regime, in the sense that the strong model acquires the target feature direction through W2S training, rather than having it given a priori. Moreover, W2S preserves pre-trained off-target features, whereas standard supervised fine-tuning causes catastrophic forgetting when off-target feature directions are correlated with the target's. Numerical experiments on synthetic data confirm our theoretical results.
